items.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: Ellington and Dizzy Gillespie and Max Roach

ctx.x: Yeah the first time I saw jazz is America’s classical music was in the context of another person saying, “Please, let’s not call it that. Do you want it to be treated like classical music is treated?” Do you want it to be shown only — I mean the whole routine.

Yeah. And let’s not forget you know that Ellington and Dizzy Gillespie and Max Roach and Fletcher and many other people wanted to get rid of the word “jazz” early on. But that’s not so much about my biography. But, but these are important things to talk about. I mean frankly, Monk, I mean if this was another context I would love to interview — right now I’m kind of dying to know what you think about all these things. No, but I mean it. I’m serious. Because you’ve taught and you’ve been around for a long time and…

Well don’t you usually think that, usually explaining things and putting them in context historical and otherwise is usually left to the people who are not doing it. The people that are doing it think less about where is my work fitting in to the timeline and the whole development thing. They’re doing it because they’re driven, and then years later it will get sorted out but not by them but by somebody else.
